As the process relies on electrical desorption, the carbon intensity of the electricity source is the primary driver of the overall emissions. With the current grid mix, the process results in net-positive CO₂ emissions due to its high electricity demand. Technology Maturation Plan Through the bench scale testing of the structured sorbent filter, TRL 4 was successfully demonstrated for this technology. Further maturation of this technology requires improvements in the structured sorbent manufacturing that can be tested in larger scale demonstrations. This would be achieved through identifying manufacturing features that limited sorbent performance and stability, and implementing manufacturing improvements to address these issues. In parallel, continued sorbent composition screening will be conducted using Susteon’s in-house synthesis and screening expertise to identify sorbent candidates that improve on the performance of ECCOsorb-T1, which can further reduce the cost of capture in accordance with TEA findings.
